one_line: Third Sikh Guru of Goindval, builder of the baoli and advocate of social equality.

appearance.age_look: Appears in his mid-70s, slightly stooped yet sturdy, with a lean elder’s build that still suggests quiet physical resilience.
appearance.face: Oval face with a warm wheat-brown Punjabi complexion, fine age lines at the eyes and forehead, high cheekbones, a long straight nose, serene deep-set eyes with dark irises, and a calm, compassionate default expression that softens into a gentle, knowing half-smile.
appearance.hair: Long white hair fully wrapped in a simple off-white cotton turban tied low and smooth without ornament, with a neatly gathered long white beard parted slightly in the middle and tucked forward over his chest, moustache blended into the beard, and a small plain under-turban knot subtly visible at the front.
appearance.costume: He wears a knee-length, long-sleeved off-white cotton kurta with a straight simple collar and side slits, over loose off-white cotton churidar-style trousers; around his shoulders is a soft, unpatterned light-ochre cotton chadar draped from the left shoulder across the chest and wrapped around his back, its edge falling over his right forearm; at his waist is a narrow pale-brown woven cloth girdle barely visible under the chadar; his feet are in plain brown leather Punjabi juttis with slightly upturned toes; textiles are matte, handwoven-looking, with very subtle, almost invisible vertical weave lines and no embroidery or decoration, embodying simplicity and humility appropriate to a mid-16th-century rural Punjabi spiritual leader.
appearance.signature: A smooth, well-used wooden walking staff about shoulder height, medium-brown in colour with a slightly darker knobbed top, no metal fittings or carvings, always held in his right hand or resting lightly beside him to evoke both his age and his role as a guiding support.

ref_desc: Guru Amar Das is an elderly wheat-brown Punjabi man with an oval, lined yet gentle face, deep-set dark eyes, a long white beard and moustache, a simple off-white turban, a plain off-white kurta and churidar, a light-ochre chadar, brown juttis, and a smooth medium-brown wooden walking staff.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style character sheet of Guru Amar Das as an elderly but quietly strong Punjabi man: he has a wheat-brown complexion, an oval face with soft age lines, deep-set dark eyes, a serene gentle expression, and a long white beard that parts slightly and flows neatly over his chest with the moustache blending into it. His long white hair is fully wrapped in a simple off-white cotton turban tied low and smooth without ornament, with a small under-turban knot subtly visible at the front. He wears a knee-length, long-sleeved off-white cotton kurta with a straight simple collar and side slits, over loose off-white churidar-style trousers. Around his shoulders is a soft, unpatterned light-ochre cotton chadar draped from his left shoulder across his chest and around his back, its edge hanging over his right forearm, suggesting quiet dignity and humility. A narrow pale-brown woven cloth girdle at his waist is only faintly visible. On his feet are plain brown leather Punjabi juttis with slightly upturned toes. In his right hand he holds his signature smooth medium-brown wooden walking staff, about shoulder height with a slightly darker rounded knob at the top and no metal fittings, sometimes resting lightly by his side. Use a subdued palette of off-white, light ochre, medium brown, wheat-brown skin tone, and dark brown for eyes and staff, and present him from multiple angles to clearly show his face, turban, beard, draped chadar, simple garments, juttis, and walking staff, all in a modest, historically grounded 16th-century Punjabi look with clean shonen-anime linework.
